title: Shotset sanitization protocols
content:
Notes to self:
- Goal: produce a lightweight, repeatable pipeline to "sanitize" few-shot exemplars (shotsets) before they are used in customer-facing prompts or released in template libraries.
- Context: lots of subtle leakage and temporal anchors creeping into exemplars; also style/label drift across exemplars that confuses the model. Need heuristics + quick tests.

What I mean by "shotset":
- A curated set of 3-12 exemplars used inline for few-shot prompting (formatting + content examples). Not a training dataset.

Primary goals for sanitization:
1) remove direct sensitive / PII leaks
2) remove temporal anchors (dates, version numbers) that cause brittleness
3) unify style/labeling conventions so exemplars signal consistent instruction-following behavior
4) remove adversarial or ambiguous examples that increase hallucination risk
5) tag or replace rare domain jargon that's unnecessary for a broad template

Sanitization checklist (fast pass):
- PII/Emails/Secrets: regex scan for email patterns, long hex strings, private URLs, API keys. Remove or redact.
- Temporal anchors: years, "last week", version strings (v1.2), timestamps -> replace with placeholders like <RECENT_DATE>
- Named entities: companies, person names -> consider replacing with generic tokens unless exemplar is testing NER behavior.
- Label consistency: ensure answer/label format is identical across shots (e.g., always bulleted list vs paragraph). If not, normalize or drop offending shots.
- Instruction mismatch: confirm each exemplar actually follows the instruction prompt in top. Remove examples that contradict the instruction.
- Toxicity filter: run a toxicity classifier and flag anything above threshold for review.
- Hallucination triggers: sentences like "according to our database" or "the system knows" flagged for rewrite.

Heuristics for candidate removal (when unsure):
- If an exemplar requires domain-specific context not present in the instruction, remove it.
- If an exemplar contains multiple correct answers or ambiguous labeling, remove.
- Prefer fewer, cleaner shots than more noisy shots. 3-5 good shots beats 10 mixed-quality ones.

Filtering pipeline (stages):
1) Automated scans: regex PII, date/year extraction, domain-n-gram anomaly detection, toxicity score. Produce a report with flags.
2) Format normalizer: canonicalize spacing, list styles, quote/escape policy (consistent quoting).
3) Semantic checks: "does each exemplar obey the instruction?" (heuristic matching via embedding similarity between instruction and exemplar context + exemplar answer).
4) Manual triage: reviewer (owner or triage pool) resolves flagged shots.
5) Snapshot + provenance: store sanitized shotset with metadata (original ids, redaction notes, reviewer initials).

Quick extraction rules to implement (regex + heuristics):
- EMAIL: [\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}
- API KEYS: 20+ char hex/base64-like strings -> redact
- DATES: (20|19)\d{2}|\b\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{2,4}\b -> replace with <DATE>
- VERSION: v?\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)? -> <VERSION>
- URL: https?://[^\s]+ -> <URL>

Example few-shot template (pre-sanitization):
Instruction: "Summarize the customer complaint and propose next steps."
Shot A: "[Jane Doe, Acme Corp] 2024-11-30 - "Customer said payment failed; invoice #INV-9999; see link https://acme.internal/123" -> Proposed: "Escalate to billing, retry card."
Shot B: "Customer: john@acme.com says 'site is slow' on v2.1.3" -> Proposed: "Scale up instances; check DB slow queries."

After sanitization (example):
Instruction: "Summarize the customer complaint and propose next steps."
Shot A: "[Customer] <DATE> - "Customer reported payment failed; invoice <INVOICE_ID>" -> Proposed: "Escalate to billing; request transaction logs."
Shot B: "[Customer] <DATE> - "Customer reported site performance issues on <VERSION>" -> Proposed: "Investigate DB queries; consider horizontal scaling."

Failure cases observed (field notes):
- Replacing company names sometimes removed critical context that the model relied on to choose domain-specific action (e.g., 'Acme' signaled B2B subscription vs consumer). Tradeoff: when to preserve domain labels? Maybe keep as "<COMPANY:SMB>" vs "<COMPANY:ENTERPRISE>".
- Over-normalizing answer format flattened diversity and reduced model's creativity on ambiguous asks. Need to balance consistency with allowable variant forms.
- Toxicity filter (aggressive) removed examples that contained profanity used purposely to test moderation paths. Need a separate 'adversarial' shotset tag so we don't silently drop these from production templates.

Experiment snippets (quick results):
- Experiment 1 (2025-01-15): 5-shot unsanitized vs 4-shot sanitized on small support ticket summarization set (n=200).
  - Unsanitized: precision@1 for correct action 0.69
  - Sanitized: precision@1 0.75
  - Notes: sanitized reduced hallucinated references to internal ticket ids.
- Experiment 2 (2025-01-22): removed temporal anchors only (dates) vs full sanitization.
  - Dates-only: marginal improvement +0.03 F1
  - Full: +0.07 F1; so multiple factors help.

Quick rubric for evaluation:
- Fidelity (does the summary/action match gold): 0/1
- Hallucination rate (mentions of non-present artifacts): % per response
- Instruction conformance (format): % matching desired answer style (list/paragraph)
- Safety flags per 1k responses: number of toxic or PII-leaking replies

Operational notes / TODOs:
- [ ] Build a small Python script to run the regex + embed-sim checks (hook into prompt-scripts repo). See GH: redwood-inference/prompt-scripts#142.
- [ ] Add provenance metadata when sanitizing (date, reviewer, original_shot_id).
- [ ] Create a separate "adversarial" shotset registry to keep intentionally toxic/PII-laden examples for robustness testing (do not include in customer templates).
- [ ] Add unit tests: pass a shotset, expect sanitized.json with exact redaction rules. Minimal CI check.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- When to replace named entities vs keep them? Suggest policy: if exemplar is testing entity-handling, keep with annotation; otherwise redact.
- How to handle multi-turn exemplars (dialogue) where redaction in one turn breaks coherence? Maybe replace with consistent tokens across turns (PersonA/PersonB).
- Thresholds for toxicity: keep a log of dropped examples with scores so we can audit false positives.

Personal notes:
- Keep the hygiene pipeline lightweight; aim for ~1-2 min human triage per 10-shot set.
- Make sanitized shotsets discoverable in the template library with tags: "sanitized-v1, provenance:maya-2025-01"

Scribbles for implementation (functions):
- detect_pii(text) -> list(flags)
- normalize_format(text, style) -> text
- check_instruction_alignment(instruction, exemplar) -> score (embedding sim)

Short-term next steps (this sprint):
1) Prototype regex-based sanitizer + format normalizer (Jon)
2) Add embedding-based instruction alignment check (Priya)
3) Run on 50 high-use templates and produce a report (me)

If this lands well, we can fold into the Console as a per-template sanitization badge for template creators.

End of notes.

-- maya
